results.content: > We add the information their study provides with to our article. Usage of the verb "provide". In the first, the material provided is the object, in the second the recipient is the object. > We add the information the study provides us with to our article. > We add the information the study provides to our article. In AmE, you can indeed say *"We add the information the study provides us to our article."* See Wikipedia and this ELU.SE question. Indeed, it would be simpler (and clearer) to say "We add the information *provided by* the study to our article". > We add the information the study provides *us* with to our article. In your original sentence, the prepositional phrase "with information" didn't modify any words. In your example *with information* doesn't modify *us* (in the way it would in *They saw us with the information*); rather, it specifies part of the activity of providing. 16") Usage of the verb "provide".
